rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for the animal itself.

example.english: That bear at the zoo is very big.
example.jyutping: dung6 mat6 jyun4 go2 zek3 hung4 hou2 daai6

rows.note: Use this for the all-purpose idea of enduring or tolerating pain, hardship, or scrutiny.

example.jyutping: ngo5 jan2 m4 dou2 ni1 zung2 tung3

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb for carrying or bringing something, including carrying weapons or symbols.

example.english: They bear arms while serving in the military.
example.traditional: 佢哋服兵役嗰陣會帶武器。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 fuk6 bing1 jik6 go2 zan6 wui5 daai3 mou5 hei3

rows.note: Use this for a thing, task, or chore that is a hassle, rather than for an animal, person, or investor.

example.english: Doing this report is a real bear.
example.traditional: 搞呢份報告真係一件麻煩嘢。
example.jyutping: gaau2 ni1 fan6 bou3 gou3 zan1 hai6 jat1 gin6 maa4 faan4 je5

rows.note: Use this all-purpose verb when something has or displays a mark, appearance, name, reputation, or bodily feature.
Use this for taking on a physical load or being responsible for a cost, liability, or responsibility.

example.traditional: 呢筆維修費由我哋承擔。
example.jyutping: ni1 bat1 wai4 sau1 fai3 jau4 ngo5 dei6 sing4 daam1

rows.note: Use this colloquial label for a rough or uncouth person, not for the animal.

example.english: That bear of a guy is yelling at people again.
example.jyutping: go2 go3 hung4 jan4 jau6 hai2 dou6 naau6 jan4

rows.note: Use this financial term for an investor who expects prices to fall and sells accordingly.

example.english: I'm a bear; with the market so high, I think it will fall soon.
example.traditional: 我係淡友，見個市咁高，我估佢快跌。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai6 daam6 jau5 gin3 go3 si5 gam3 gou1 ngo5 gu2 keoi5 faai3 dit3
